# Grid headers can keep their old aria-colindex after a reorder

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderGroups.spec.mjs:810` failed in `e2e-engine (8/15)` of run 44466942051 (job 135367299773). That arm releases a group during its held drag start. The run was on #21424's head `a63b91a152`, a calendar change unrelated to the grid. The drop's order was right, but `Q3`'s last leaf could not be found by its `aria-colindex`. It stayed missing through the extra 10 s that #21421 added:

```
{"index":5,"text":"Q3","left":631,"right":1081,"leafLeft":631,"leafRight":null}
```

**Reproduced locally.** The release arm stalled in 1 of 25 runs with the browser pinned to efficiency cores (`taskpolicy -c background`). CPU throttling of the page alone gave 0 stalls in 32 runs. The DOM inventory at the stall shows that no header is missing. The three moved headers kept their old index, and the three they passed took the new ones:

| Header | Jul | Aug | Sep | Apr | May | Jun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| position | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
| `aria-colindex` in the DOM | 8 | 9 | 10 | 8 | 9 | 10 |

So `aria-colindex` 5, 6 and 7 name no header. The spec finds group edges by this index, and a screen reader announces the column position from it.

## The Problem

After a reorder, the grid renumbers its headers. It writes `aria-colindex` straight into each header button's vdom, then ships the writes with the toolbar's own update at `updateDepth = 2`. These writes are silent: no header requests its own update for them.

When one header's own update merges into that toolbar cycle, `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` builds the cycle sparse. It expands only the merged headers and leaves every other header as a reference. Those headers keep their old index in the DOM until their own next update. After a drop, nothing sends one.

A held drag start packs the drop's style restores and the renumbering into one window, so the e2e arm shows the defect first. The path is the same for every drop and every region re-sync.

**Deterministic red on `dev`**, through the production re-sync path. The setup is a mounted unit-test grid driven by `Wrapper#applyColumnButtonOrder`:
- It swaps the two center headers.
- In the same pass, one header's text update merges into the toolbar's cycle.
- The cycle ran at depth 2, sparse, with merged ids `[city]`.
- Afterwards both headers' vnodes read `aria-colindex` 3, while `name`'s vdom holds 4.

With `denseUpdate` set on the toolbar, the cycle ships both indexes.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The writers:**
  - `src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:555-559`, the drop in `processDragEnd`.
  - `src/grid/header/Wrapper.mjs:151-168`, `applyColumnButtonOrder` after a column mutation.
  - `src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:297`, `createItems` for new items. This one is safe, because children without a vnode always expand.
- **The sparse rule:** `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:403-407`.
- **Design authority:** `denseUpdate`'s JSDoc, `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:43-49`: *"True for one update cycle: the owner changed descendants silently within its `updateDepth`, so the cycle ships that subtree whole instead of sparse, even when children merge into it."* The header writers change descendants silently and do not set it.
- **The same class was fixed per site before:**
  - `component.Base#hide()`, #19402.
  - `form.Fieldset#updateLegend()`, #19404. #19404 kept "making `denseUpdate` implicit for every owner-raised depth" out of scope as an engine design change.

## The Fix

`grid.header.Toolbar` owns the write in one method, `syncAriaColumnIndexes()`:
- It writes each header's grid-wide index: toolbar index + `ariaColumnOffset` + 1.
- When an index changed, it raises the next cycle to depth 2 and marks it `denseUpdate`.
- It returns whether an index changed.

The SortZone drop, the Wrapper re-sync and `createItems` call it, and their inline loops go. That leaves one writer for the invariant instead of three.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit spec renumbers the headers through `Wrapper#applyColumnButtonOrder` while one header's own update merges into the toolbar's cycle. It reads every header's **vnode** index (what reached the DOM), never its vdom. It is red on `dev` and green with the fix.
- [ ] The drop renumbers through `syncAriaColumnIndexes()`, pinned in `test/playwright/unit/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] No inline `aria-colindex` write remains in the three writers.
- [ ] `HeaderGroups.spec.mjs` passes. Its release arm passes a 25-run efficiency-core battery with no stall (the sighting on `dev` was 1 in 25).
- [ ] The unit suite stays green.

## Out of Scope

- **`grid.header.Toolbar#afterSetSortable` and `grid.Body#updateCellPositions`.** Both are the same class, both were measured red since filing, and both are filed as #21451. `#afterSetUseTriStateSorting` changes no header vdom.
- **The header filter field's `removeDom` in `grid.header.Button`.** It may change a child silently, but it is unmeasured here, so no claim is made.
- **An engine rule that infers `denseUpdate` from an owner-raised depth.** This is the design change #19404 declined.

## Avoided Traps

- **Waiting longer in the spec.** The stall never heals: no later update reaches the stale headers.
- **Raising the toolbar to `updateDepth = -1`.** That also ships every header's filter subtree, where dense at depth 2 is the documented minimum.
- **Asserting `button.vdom['aria-colindex']`.** The vdom always holds the new index. The defect is only visible in the vnode and the DOM.
